text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: C:/Users/KRK/GitStore/entire-brain/docs/linear-integration-plan.md
+# Linear integration proposal
+
+Status: design proposal, not implemented. Inspected 2026-09-17 against the
+working checkout and freshly fetched `origin/main` (`34fb3e04`).
+
+## Intended outcome
+
+Support one workflow across three capabilities:
+
+1. Search Linear issues, project context, and comments alongside repository memory.
+2. Start work on an issue with relevant code, prior decisions, sessions, and tests.
+3. Create issues and publish selected findings, progress, and status changes to Linear.
+
+Example: an agent starts ENG-123, reads its acceptance criteria, retrieves an earlier
+failed approach from Brain, implements and tests a fix, then posts the result with
+the relevant commit/PR links. A later agent can retrieve that issue and its outcome.
+
+## What exists
+
+No native Linear client, authentication flow, issue store, or synchronization
+command was found in the implementation or product documentation on either revision.
+Benchmark material mentioning Linear describes captured conversations, not a connector.
+
+Existing building blocks:
+
+- `internal/cli/mcp.go`: Brain's MCP server, including task briefs and retrieval.
+- `internal/cli/retrieve.go` and `retrieve_cmd.go`: unified retrieval and source selectors.
+- `internal/cli/doc.go`: local seed-document chunking and indexing.
+- `internal/cli/agent_surface.go`: task briefs combining repository context.
+- `internal/factmerge/record.go`: durable facts with session/commit/checkpoint anchors.
+- `internal/cli/agent_policy.go`: local-only/no-egress policy.
+
+These are candidate extension points, not a completed dependency-impact audit.
+The local development binary can run a brief but lacks `capabilities`; its selected
+repository store reports missing seed, session, semantic, history, fact, and doc
+sources. Consequently, no historical rationale is inferred from its empty brief.
+
+## Architecture
+
+Use Linear's official MCP server for an initial agent-operated workflow. It already
+supports reading, creating, and updating issues, projects, and comments. The Codex
+OAuth login authorizes that client; it does not authenticate Brain or create a local
+issue index. [Linear MCP documentation](https://linear.app/docs/mcp)
+
+For a native connector, use Linear's GraphQL API behind a small Go client with
+separate read and write operations. Brain should own its OAuth application and
+credential lifecycle, with credentials held in an OS credential store. Do not read
+Codex's private credential files or assume its MCP token is reusable for GraphQL.
+See [GraphQL](https://linear.app/developers/graphql) and
+[OAuth](https://linear.app/developers/oauth-2-0-authentication).
+
+Store scoped issue snapshots locally, separately from authored facts. Use workspace
+ID plus immutable issue UUID as identity; retain the display identifier, canonical
+URL, team/project IDs, status, description, comments, source update time, fetch time,
+and content hash. Configure an explicit repository-to-team/project mapping.
+
+Add a distinct retrieval source, initially opt-in, with links and freshness on
+results. An issue saying a fix is complete is external evidence, not verification
+that a commit implements it. Extend fact provenance only when supporting facts
+derived from external snapshots; existing session anchors cannot honestly represent
+an issue URL. Preserve an immutable snapshot reference for any derived fact.
+
+## Delivery sequence
+
+### 1. One-issue workflow through the agent
+
+Connect both MCP servers in the agent host. Fetch one issue and its relevant
+comments, query Brain using the issue's actual problem and acceptance criteria,
+then assemble a cited task brief. Link explicit issue IDs/URLs to sessions and
+commits; inferred associations must remain distinguishable from explicit links.
+
+Create a follow-up issue or post a concise finding through Linear MCP when the
+user requests it. This provides early value across all three capabilities, but
+does not yet provide persistent Linear search inside Brain.
+
+### 2. Native ingestion and retrieval
+
+Introduce proposed modules `internal/linear` (API/auth boundary) and
+`internal/issues` (snapshot storage, identity, synchronization state, and links),
+then wire them into CLI, MCP, retrieval, task briefs, and source-health reporting.
+Final placement should follow a dependency audit on a fresh mainline checkout.
+
+Start with explicit, bounded sync for one selected project/team. Page issues and
+comments independently; checkpoint progress only after committed local writes.
+Handle GraphQL errors even on HTTP 200, rate limits, retries, and interrupted runs.
+Polling should use incremental updates with an overlap window and deduplication;
+it also needs periodic reconciliation for deletions, moves, and lost access.
+Archived issues require deliberate handling because ordinary paginated API results
+hide them by default. [Linear API guidance](https://linear.app/developers/graphql)
+
+Keep offline search available and label stale snapshots. On known removal or loss
+of access, suppress affected current results and invalidate derived indexes and
+facts as appropriate. A local-only client cannot discover revocation while offline;
+define a freshness/retention policy rather than claiming immediate revocation.
+
+### 3. Native write-back
+
+Support issue creation, comments, and selected issue-field updates. Keep a local
+operation journal with target workspace/issue, intended changes, payload hash,
+result identifiers, and outcome. Re-read mutable issue state before applying
+updates and report conflicts. Reconcile ambiguous timeouts before retrying creates
+or comments; do not assume the API supplies universal idempotency semantics.
+
+Send the requested summary and relevant links. Exporting raw sessions or unrelated
+repository context must be a separate explicit action. Reuse Brain's no-egress
+policy for every network operation, and treat imported issue text as untrusted
+source data. Do not allow an issue body to authorize writes or tool execution.
+
+### 4. Continuous updates
+
+Add signed webhooks only when an online receiver is available. Validate signatures
+and timestamps, deduplicate delivery IDs, and tolerate out-of-order events. Keep
+reconciliation for missed events. Linear documents webhook events and verification
+in its [webhook guide](https://linear.app/developers/webhooks).
+
+A local laptop should work with explicit sync first. Windows background scheduling
+needs its own implementation; the inspected Brain binary reports its existing
+watcher manager unsupported on Windows.
+
+## Proposed user surface
+
+These commands are illustrative and do not exist yet:
+
+```text
+entire brain linear connect
+entire brain linear sync --project <project>
+entire brain search "retry regression" --source issue
+entire brain brief --issue ENG-123
+entire brain linear create --title "Follow-up" --body-file issue.md
+entire brain linear comment ENG-123 --body-file findings.md
+entire brain linear update ENG-123 --state <state>
+```
+
+## Acceptance checks
+
+- Import a paginated issue/comment fixture twice without duplicates or missed pages.
+- Retrieve imported evidence offline with the correct workspace, URL, and timestamps.
+- Build a bounded issue brief that cites both issue evidence and repository evidence.
+- Test updates, archived/deleted/moved issues, lost access, and partial sync recovery.
+- Prevent cross-workspace results and keep credentials out of logs and snapshots.
+- Verify no-egress blocks every connector network path.
+- Exercise a timed-out write and prove reconciliation prevents a duplicate comment.
+- Verify existing retrieval behavior and MCP contracts remain compatible.
+- Run a live round trip on a specifically selected test issue before broader rollout.
+
+Recommended first implementation milestone: one issue imported, searchable and
+usable in a brief, followed by one explicitly requested comment with a recorded
+write receipt. Broaden scope after this complete path works.
*** End Patch"));

content.text:
The plan now covers all three capabilities. I recommend making the first milestone a complete round trip: import one issue, retrieve it through Brain, use it in a task brief, then post a requested finding back to Linear.

The main design gap is provenance: Brain’s current fact anchors point to sessions and commits. Linear evidence needs its own issue identity, source URL, snapshot, and freshness metadata.

content.text:
**Brain doesn’t currently have a native Linear integration.** I checked this checkout and freshly fetched `origin/main`. Our OAuth login connects Codex to Linear; it doesn’t populate Brain’s memory.

I wrote a [build proposal](C:/Users/KRK/GitStore/entire-brain/docs/linear-integration-plan.md) covering all three capabilities:

| Capability | Proposed behavior |
|---|---|
| Searchable memory | Import selected issues and comments with source links and freshness |
| Issue-aware agents | Combine issue requirements with Brain’s decisions, sessions, code, and tests |
| Write-back | Create issues, post findings, and update status with recorded outcomes |

**I’d start with one complete round trip:** import an issue → search it in Brain → generate a task brief → post a requested finding back.

Linear’s [official MCP server](https://linear.app/docs/mcp) supports the initial agent workflow. Persistent synchronization would use a native GraphQL connector with its own OAuth credentials.

The key work is issue storage, external-source provenance, retrieval integration, and reliable synchronization. The proposal includes implementation stages and acceptance checks. Only the proposal was added; no integration code or Linear records were changed.
Let's plan deeper.

I’ll refine the proposal into an implementation-ready plan, starting with authentication, issue storage, and how Linear context enters task briefs. Then we’ll settle the product choices that affect the design.

content.text:
The repo has retrieval and task-brief foundations we can extend. It has no reusable OAuth or credential-store layer, so a native connector would need that infrastructure too.

Three choices will determine the scope: whether v1 is a native Brain feature, how much Linear data it retains, and when agents may write back.

questions.question: What should the first release deliver, with all three capabilities included?

options.label: Native Brain feature (Recommended)
options.description: Build persistent issue memory, issue-aware briefs, and write-back into Brain’s CLI and MCP tools.

options.label: Agent workflow first
options.description: Use Linear MCP alongside Brain, adding only a small import/link layer before building a native connector.

options.label: Hosted team integration
options.description: Build shared synchronization and webhook infrastructure for a team from the start.

questions.question: How much Linear context should Brain retain by default?

options.label: Selected projects (Recommended)
options.description: Map repositories to selected Linear projects and retain their issues, comments, and project descriptions.

options.label: Only linked issues
options.description: Retain issues explicitly selected or referenced during repository work, fetching related context on demand.

options.label: Whole selected teams
options.description: Index all issues and project context from selected teams for broader planning and discovery.

questions.question: When should agents create issues, post comments, or change Linear fields?

options.label: On user instruction (Recommended)
options.description: An authorized task can include writes; background sync stays read-only and adds no approval step.

options.label: Preview every write
options.description: Prepare the exact change and require a separate confirmation before sending it.

options.label: Configurable automation
options.description: Allow configured events, such as task completion, to post updates or change state automatically.

content.text:
We’ll start with an agent workflow, retain context from selected projects, and write back only as part of a user-authorized task.

That lets us use the Linear login already managed by the agent host. Brain’s first addition can focus on importing issue snapshots, retrieving them, and linking them to repository work, without building its own OAuth client yet.

content.text:
The first release will be host-neutral and evidence-focused. Any agent with both MCP servers can fetch a Linear issue, retain its source text in Brain, and build a brief from it. Starting or resuming issue work will refresh that issue; project-wide refresh will run on request.

Two remaining choices affect everyday use: whether imported issues appear in ordinary Brain queries, and which Linear changes the workflow supports in v1.

questions.question: After a project is connected, should its imported Linear context appear in ordinary Brain searches and task briefs?

options.label: Include by default (Recommended)
options.description: Blend relevant issue evidence into normal retrieval and briefs, with clear Linear citations and freshness.

options.label: Only when requested
options.description: Include Linear context only with an issue reference or an explicit issue-source filter.

questions.question: Which user-requested Linear changes should the v1 workflow cover?

options.label: Core issue actions (Recommended)
options.description: Create issues, post comments, and update status, assignee, priority, labels, and project.

options.label: Comments and creation
options.description: Create follow-up issues and post findings, leaving existing issue fields unchanged.

We’ve settled the product scope. Imported Linear evidence will join normal searches and briefs, while the agent uses Linear MCP for the agreed issue actions.

The import contract needs one important safeguard: it must distinguish a complete snapshot from a partial fetch. Missing comments must not be treated as deleted comments, and an interrupted project refresh must not make old data look current. I’ll also keep Brain’s own retrieval offline; network refresh remains an agent workflow step.

<proposed_plan>
# Linear-backed memory and issue workflows for Brain

## 1. Outcome and release boundary

Build a **host-neutral agent workflow** that connects Linear’s existing MCP server with Brain’s local memory.

The first release must support this complete sequence:

1. Select Linear projects for a repository.
2. Import their active issues and issues completed or canceled within the last 90 days, including comments.
3. Find imported evidence through ordinary Brain searches and task briefs.
4. Refresh an issue when starting or resuming work on it.
5. Combine its requirements with repository decisions, sessions, code context, and tests.
6. Perform user-requested Linear actions and retain the resulting links and receipts.

**Agreed defaults**

- Selected projects define the import scope.
- Imported evidence participates in normal retrieval.
- Older issues can be fetched explicitly when referenced.
- Writes require user instruction, but no additional confirmation step.
- Supported writes: create issues, post comments, and update status, assignee, priority, labels, and project.
- Store source evidence; automatic extraction of durable facts is deferred.

This release excludes native Linear OAuth, background synchronization, webhooks, project-management mutations, and hosted shared storage. The agent host owns Linear authentication and remote tool execution. Brain receives no Linear credentials.

## 2. Architecture and local data

### Separate remote access from memory

Use three components:

- **Linear MCP:** reads and writes remote Linear objects.
- **Agent workflow:** selects projects, fetches pages, imports evidence, requests Brain context, and performs authorized writes.
- **Brain issue layer:** validates and stores snapshots, indexes evidence, tracks work links, and records operation outcomes.

Publish a generic workflow document describing required tool capabilities and their sequence. Hosts discover Linear’s actual tool names and schemas; instructions must not assume a particular host or server prefix.

### Repository-scoped storage

Add an `internal/issues` package for provider-independent records and persistence. Keep CLI/MCP adapters in the existing CLI package. Do not introduce a native Linear HTTP client.

Store records under the repository’s Brain directory, outside the Git working tree:

- Connection metadata: workspace identity and selected project IDs.
- Immutable, content-addressed snapshots.
- An atomically updated index of current records.
- Import-run progress and completeness.
- Explicit links to sessions, checkpoints, commits, and PR URLs.
- Write-operation receipts.
- Rebuildable lexical and embedding indexes.

Use workspace UUID plus object UUID as identity. Display identifiers such as `ENG-123` are aliases, never storage keys.

Retain project descriptions, issue fields, and individual comments. Each record includes its canonical URL, source update time, local observation time, content hash, and completeness information. Preserve fetched text without rewriting it into a summary. Attachments remain links.

### Import correctness

Define a versioned import envelope containing workspace, import-run ID, batch ID, and typed project/issue/comment records.

- Limit each batch to 100 records and 2 MiB; reject oversized input without partial writes.
- Retrying the same batch is idempotent.
- Reject workspace/project mismatches and malformed identities.
- Publish snapshots and current pointers atomically under Brain’s write lock.
- Ignore older revisions when updating current pointers; report equal-timestamp content conflicts.
- Mark missing or truncated fields explicitly.
- Track issue and comment pagination separately.
- Never infer deletion from an absent record or interrupted fetch.
- Only explicit removal/inaccessibility evidence suppresses a record.
- Completed project imports describe the requested time window, not the entire project history.

Project imports are resumable and run only on request. Unsupported MCP filters may be applied locally after pagination; unsupported archived access must be reported as a coverage limitation.

Disconnecting a project removes its evidence from retrieval immediately. An explicit purge removes its stored snapshots and derived indexes.

## 3. Public interfaces and retrieval

### CLI and MCP

Add a provider-neutral `issues` command group and equivalent MCP tools:

| CLI | MCP | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `issues configure --input <file>` | `brain_issues_configure` | Bind workspace and selected projects |
| `issues import --input <file>` | `brain_issues_import` | Import bounded evidence batches and progress |
| `issues status` | `brain_issues_status` | Inspect bindings, coverage, freshness, and resumable runs |
| `issues link --input <file>` | `brain_issues_link` | Link an issue to repository work |
| `issues operation --input <file>` | `brain_issues_operation` | Record intended writes and observed outcomes |
| `issues disconnect --project <id> [--purge]` | `brain_issues_disconnect` | Disable a project and optionally purge its evidence |

CLI inputs accept `-` for stdin. CLI and MCP use the same validation and persistence functions. Mutating tools must be described as local mutations, not read-only tools.

Extend existing interfaces:

- `search/query/vsearch --source issue`
- `get/multi-get` support issue-evidence IDs.
- `brief --issue <identifier-or-URL>` and an equivalent optional MCP argument.
- Add issue-source health and coverage to status/doctor.
- Make the brief’s task text optional only when an issue supplies it.

Use separate addressable IDs for projects, issues, and comments. Default IDs resolve current evidence; returned snapshot references identify the exact revision used.

### Ranking and brief behavior

Add issue evidence as another ranked source in the existing retrieval fusion. Include it in default queries only for configured projects.

- Use lexical ranking immediately, with a fallback when SQLite FTS is unavailable.
- Use Brain’s existing embedding abstraction and source-specific cache for semantic retrieval.
- Without embeddings, hybrid retrieval includes lexical issue hits; issue-only semantic requests report unavailable capability.
- Invalidate embeddings by content hash.
- Group issue descriptions and comments by issue to prevent long threads dominating results.
- Return canonical links, observation times, completeness, and stale-data caveats.

Ordinary briefs select relevant issue evidence within existing output budgets. An explicitly requested issue is pinned to the brief, alongside related repository evidence. Preserve the distinction between source assertions and verified implementation behavior.

Brain queries remain offline. The agent refreshes the issue first when starting or resuming work. If that refresh fails, cached evidence remains available with an explicit warning. Treat observations older than 24 hours as stale by default.

Do not alter durable-fact anchors in this release. Issue evidence is a separate source.

## 4. Agent workflow and write-back

### Starting work

The generic workflow must:

1. Check that Brain and Linear capabilities are available.
2. Resolve the requested issue within the configured workspace and projects.
3. Fetch current issue details and paginate its comments.
4. Import the exact available source evidence, recording incomplete fetches.
5. Request an issue-aware Brain brief.
6. Retrieve supporting records as needed.
7. Record explicit session/commit/checkpoint/PR associations when those identifiers are available.

Do not invent repository associations from similarity alone. An issue outside selected projects requires explicit inclusion; it must not silently expand project scope.

Project import uses the same path, with bounded batches and progress receipts. It includes all active issues plus recently completed/canceled issues. Fetch project descriptions and issue comments; retain older explicitly referenced issues independently of the initial window.

### Performing requested changes

Remote mutations remain Linear MCP calls made by the agent host.

Before writing, the workflow resolves the exact target and field IDs and reads current values. It records a pending local operation containing the target, requested action, payload hash, and relevant pre-write values.

After writing:

- Record returned object IDs, URLs, timestamps, and outcome.
- Re-fetch affected evidence and import it into Brain.
- If the write succeeded but local import failed, report those outcomes separately.
- Never retry an ambiguous create/comment automatically. Inspect Linear for the result; leave the operation `unknown` when it cannot be resolved confidently.
- For field updates, re-read changed fields and stop on detected conflicting changes. Do not claim atomic conflict prevention unless the remote API supports it.

Operation receipts are observations, not proof that Brain independently enforced user authorization. Authorization belongs to the host and the user’s task instructions.

Send the requested summary and relevant links. Imported issue text cannot authorize tool execution or writes. Raw transcripts are not automatically included in comments.

Honor no-egress mode in the workflow by skipping Linear calls; local import and cached retrieval remain usable. Brain cannot technically enforce another MCP server’s network policy, so document that boundary.

## 5. Delivery, validation, and acceptance

Implement on a fresh branch from current mainline. The existing proposal document is a draft to replace during implementation.

Deliver in four ordered changes:

1. **Storage and imports:** bindings, snapshot identity, atomic batches, completeness, disconnection, and status.
2. **Retrieval:** issue-source search, get, semantic indexing, citations, and issue-aware briefs.
3. **Workflow:** host-neutral instructions, project import/resume, work linking, and write-operation receipts.
4. **Compatibility and end-to-end verification:** CLI/MCP contracts, documentation, platform checks, and a live test.

Required tests:

- Repeat imports without duplicate records or revision regression.
- Interrupt pagination and resume without falsely declaring completeness.
- Preserve comments omitted by a partial fetch.
- Handle deleted, inaccessible, moved, and disconnected records.
- Isolate repositories and workspaces with colliding display identifiers.
- Retrieve exact cited snapshots offline.
- Keep results and briefs bounded for large issues and long comment threads.
- Verify lexical fallback, semantic-cache invalidation, and stale-data reporting.
- Exercise malicious issue text without following embedded instructions.
- Reconcile successful, failed, and ambiguous remote writes without blind retries.
- Preserve existing retrieval behavior when no projects are configured.
- Ensure existing publishing/bundling paths do not automatically export issue content.
- Verify Windows, macOS, and Linux storage behavior.

The source inspection and Graph impact results show that unified retrieval has many consumers, including workspace rendering and transport budgeting. Compatibility tests must cover those surfaces. Graph reported an `E_NO_GIT_HEAD` warning, so repeat impact verification on the implementation checkout before editing shared contracts.

**Release acceptance:** using any compatible agent host with both MCP servers connected, import a selected project, retrieve an issue through an ordinary Brain query, produce a cited issue-aware brief, post a user-requested comment to a designated test issue, and retrieve that confirmed outcome from Brain afterward. No Brain-owned Linear token or background service is required.
</proposed_plan>
